artboards.title: Desk — Decisions on the well's column, 1440×900
Previous pass — band version (three access levels)

annotations.text:
THE DESK, ONE SCREEN

Hero trimmed: KPI rows 188 (was 215), numeral 72, the well tighter — the height goes to the bottom cards.

Below, the columns follow the hero's own 29/45 grid: Decisions sits exactly on the Dex well's column, and the right 45 splits 1.35 : 1 between Task approvals and the Due today / Leave / Slipping stack. Four rows on each big card; every row opens in a popup (the open icon) — no inline approve/reject, since rejecting a decision deletes its tasks and belongs on the decision page.

Still 1440×900 with no scroll. The Company/You control is live.

THE TEST

Same page, three access levels. Each section is tied to a permission (decisions_approve, approvals, leave_approve, finance/ledger), so the row shortens with less access rather than leaving a hole: owner 6·2·2·2, manager 6·3·3, sales 1·1.

Worth arguing with: sales gets a fourth tile — 'Follow-ups, this week' — which is the brief's open question 4 answered from their own tasks.

STRUCTURE ONLY. These two were drawn before the Karma material was lifted, so ignore their styling; they're here for the layout argument alone.

B, One queue: no sections, one list ranked by what it blocks. Loses per-kind counts and makes the access story invisible.

C, The morning read: Dex writes the day as prose and the named things are the controls. Lives or dies on answer quality, which ASK-23 says isn't there yet.
